subject: Pathology
summary: Cancer cells acquire several biological capabilities that allow uncontrolled growth, invasion and resistance to death. Recognising these hallmarks guides diagnosis, prognosis and therapy.

sections.p: Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by clonal cell proliferation with the ability to invade surrounding tissue and metastasize. Diagnosis rests on histopathology showing atypia, mitoses and loss of normal architecture.
b: Histology confirms malignancy; immunohistochemistry helps identify tissue of origin.

sections.p: Staging uses the TNM system (Tumour size, Node involvement, Metastasis) and determines prognosis and treatment intensity.
b: Stage I–IV reflects increasing spread; higher stage = poorer survival.

sections.p: Most cancers arise from accumulated genetic alterations driven by environmental exposures, infections and inherited syndromes.
b: Tobacco, alcohol, UV light – common mutagens.
Infections: HPV, EBV, HBV/HCV, H. pylori, HIV (immune suppression).

sections.p: Patients may notice a new lump, unexplained weight loss, persistent pain, bleeding or organ‑specific symptoms (e.g., cough, hematuria).
b: Symptoms reflect tumour location and size; systemic signs suggest metastasis.

sections.p: A stepwise approach combines imaging, tissue sampling and molecular tests to define tumour type and stage.

t.b: Confirms malignancy and identifies histologic subtype; guides treatment choice.
Determines tissue of origin when primary site is unclear.
Assesses tumour size, nodal involvement and distant metastasis; essential for TNM staging.
Detects actionable mutations (e.g., EGFR, KRAS); informs targeted therapy. If unavailable, treat based on histology and stage.

sections.p: Rapid tumour growth, obstruction, bleeding, spinal cord compression or superior vena cava syndrome demand urgent intervention.
b: These complications can be life‑threatening and require immediate specialist care.

sections.p: Treatment follows a hierarchy: remove or control the tumour, then address systemic disease and supportive needs.
b: Surgery or radiotherapy for local control.
Chemotherapy (cell‑cycle inhibitors) for proliferating cells; avoid in patients with severe marrow suppression.
Targeted agents (e.g., tyrosine‑kinase inhibitors) when specific mutations are present; chosen for efficacy and lower systemic toxicity.
Immunotherapy (checkpoint inhibitors) re‑activates anti‑tumour immunity; contraindicated in uncontrolled autoimmune disease.

sections.p: Regular surveillance imaging and tumor markers detect recurrence early. Lifestyle modification and vaccination (HPV, HBV) reduce future cancer risk.
b: Screening programs (e.g., colonoscopy, mammography) are cost‑effective even in low‑resource settings.

sections.p: Benign proliferative lesions (e.g., fibroadenoma, lipoma) can mimic cancer clinically and radiologically.
b: Biopsy distinguishes benign from malignant growth.

sections.p: Tumour markers may be normal in early disease; inflammatory conditions can raise markers falsely.
b: Do not rely on a single test; correlate with imaging and pathology.

whenToSeekHelp: Sudden severe pain, unexplained bleeding, neurological deficits, signs of obstruction or sepsis.

faq.q: Why do cancers become resistant to apoptosis?
faq.a: Mutations in TP53 or over‑expression of BCL‑2 block programmed cell death, allowing survival despite DNA damage.

faq.q: What is the clinical relevance of telomerase re‑activation?
faq.a: It gives cancer cells unlimited replicative potential, contributing to tumour growth and resistance to therapy.

faq.q: How does the tumour microenvironment affect cancer progression?
faq.a: Stromal cells, immune cells and angiogenesis provide growth signals and help tumour cells invade and metastasise.

exam: List the original six hallmarks of cancer and give one molecular example for each.
Explain how the TNM staging system influences treatment decisions for solid tumours.
Describe the rationale for using targeted therapy versus conventional chemotherapy in a patient with an EGFR‑mutated lung adenocarcinoma.
